audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Renekton level 3, levels 4-5, first item and two items, while the page's own prose says 'The moment you hit 3 it flips', 'This is your lane' and 'You take over completely'. It also gave Aurora level 1, the one stage the prose concedes outright.
audit.why: Four rows contradicted the text beside them, against a 53.79% win rate over 145 games. Renekton's threat is a 300-range stun on a 16s cooldown at rank 1 with a 16s dash; once Aurora has Twofold Hex and The Weirding she is out of both ranges.
audit.corrected: Chart rebuilt to the packet chart: Renekton level 1, Aurora every row after. whys[1] already said the poke war starts at 2, so the level-2 row now agrees with it.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes listed 'Ruthless Predator online, level 6, first item' with no timing content, and no cooldown appeared anywhere in the full layer.
audit.why: His spikes are specific: 50 Fury turns Ruthless Predator into a 1.5s stun rather than 0.75s, Dominus at 6 is bonus health plus periodic fury, and his first item is his last real damage spike before base damage flatlines. Aurora's is level 3, when the second spell opens the poke war.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten with the fury threshold, Dominus and level 3; cooldowns block rebuilt on 16/14/12/10/8 and 16s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three content strings claimed Aurora's 'spirit mode lets you walk walls' and that the rift is 'untargetable to anyone outside it'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Across the Veil is a leap that leaves her invisible with bonus move speed; Between Worlds is damage, a slow, and an area she can teleport across. Neither grants terrain traversal and neither grants untargetability. The real, checkable asymmetry is that the zone slows Renekton while Aurora crosses it freely, which is what forces his Slice and Dice to start from outside.
audit.corrected: Wall-walking and untargetability removed from spikes[2], mid, late and whys[4]; replaced with the slow-versus-free-crossing asymmetry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ruthless Predator's empowered form destroys damage shields on the target, and nothing says so.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit. It does not change this lane — Aurora's kit has no shield — so by the relevance rule it stays off the page. Recording it here so the next auditor does not re-derive it.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 belong to him: a fury-empowered W (Ruthless Predator) is an extended point-blank stun and his Q (Cull the Meek) heals him through your chip, so do not walk into melee to throw a Q he can stun you out of. Last-hit at max Q range, keep your W (Across the Veil) up for his E dash, and concede a little CS rather than eat the stun. The moment you hit 3 it flips — your Q out-and-recast plus E-hop poke chips faster than his fury combo can answer, and Spirit Abjuration heals the trade back.
edits.after: Level 1 belongs to him: a fury-empowered Ruthless Predator is a 1.5s point-blank stun and Cull the Meek (7s) heals him through your chip, so do not walk into melee to throw a Q he can stun you out of. Last-hit at max Q range, keep Across the Veil up for Slice and Dice, and concede a little CS rather than eat the stun. From level 2 it flips — Twofold Hex out-and-recast plus The Weirding's hop chips faster than his fury combo can answer, and Spirit Abjuration heals the trade back.

edits.before: This is your lane. With your Q cooldown dropping and three stacks of Spirit Abjuration sustaining you, you out-poke his point-blank trades — he has to burn his E dash to even reach you, and once it is down he is a melee with no follow-up. Bait the fury-empowered W, then E-poke and Q-recast burst as his fury bar empties. At 6 the R rift slows him and your spirit mode lets you walk walls and dodge his W-Q all-in, so every fight is on your terms and your W resets on the takedown.
edits.after: This is your lane. With your Q cooldown dropping and three stacks of Spirit Abjuration sustaining you, you out-poke his 300-range trades — he has to burn Slice and Dice (16s at rank 1) to even reach you, and once it is down he is a melee with no follow-up. Bait the fury-empowered Ruthless Predator, then E-poke and Q-recast burst as his fury bar empties. At 6 the rift slows him while you cross it freely, so his all-in has to begin from outside it and every fight happens on your terms.

edits.before: You take over completely. Renekton has no sustained threat once his early fury combo stops one-shotting and his base damage flatlines — your scaled Q-recast burst out-trades anything he can do, while your R rift (untargetable to anyone outside it) and W blink let you disengage every time he commits his E and stun. Keep poking, zone him off objectives with the rift, and snowball the W-reset kills. His only path back is a levels 1-2 snowball banked before your poke turned the lane.
edits.after: You take over completely. Renekton has no sustained threat once his early fury combo stops one-shotting and his base damage flatlines — your scaled Q-recast burst out-trades anything he can do, while the rift slow and Across the Veil let you disengage every time he commits Slice and Dice and the stun. Keep poking, zone him off objectives with the rift, and snowball the kills. His only path back is a level-1 snowball banked before your poke turned the lane.

Worth a single pass across the champion. UNVERIFIED and left in place where it already existed: 'Across the Veil resets on takedown'. It is asserted repeatedly in the content layer, it is not in Riot's ability text, and I removed it from the strings I rewrote rather than re-assert it — but it is still present in wants.you[2] history and in other matchups.
